text: An abstract class defines a contract that its subclasses must fulfill, but can't be used on its own.
You inherit from ABC, the abstract base class, and mark required methods with the abstractmethod decorator.
Payment declares that every payment type must have a pay method, but gives no implementation itself.
[chuckle] Card is a concrete subclass — it actually implements pay, so it's complete and usable.
[sniff] Try to create a Payment directly, and Python refuses with a TypeError.
That's the whole point — the abstract class exists only to be extended, never instantiated raw.
It guarantees that anyone building a payment type won't forget the essential pay method.
[sigh] Card, having fulfilled the contract, works perfectly and processes the payment.
[groan] Abstract classes are how you design safe, consistent plugin systems — define the interface, enforce it everywhere.
